items.title: Replace the event-count drag/hold discriminator with a distance slop; under §S24-C the ONLY threshold the slash-vs-move classifier needs is a tiny hold slop
items.claim: Universal practice discriminates drag-from-click by DISTANCE from the down point, not by event count: Windows starts a drag only past SM_CXDRAG/SM_CYDRAG (default 4 px, DragDetect rectangle); inside the slop 'nothing happens'. pointermove dispatch is rAF-aligned (~60 Hz typical) and coalescing varies per device/browser, so a count of pointermove events measures event rate, not motion. The repo's `mouseMoving = this.mouseHoldActive && this.dragPoints.length < 4` (DuelScene.update) is exactly the fragile form: a jittery hold cancels run after 4 events regardless of distance, and the first ≤3 move events of EVERY real stroke feed `moveTargetX` — the fighter starts moving at stroke onset, which is the owner-reported 'short drags stolen for movement' bug direction. The §S24-C-consistent classifier: while held and cumulative displacement ≤ slop → movement verb (hold-run/click-destination per ledger b-1); once displacement > slop → the gesture IS a stroke, movement intent nulls for its remainder; on release, any beyond-slop stroke = slash at ANY range (PB-1/Beach S6: point-blank strokes attack). No minimum-slash-length and no range gate exist or may be added.

sources.title: What happens if I drag the mouse by exactly SM_CXDRAG? — Raymond Chen, The Old New Thing

items.adjudication_reason: DuelScene.update's `dragPoints.length < 4` heuristic contradicts ledger §S24-C A12.2 ('classification cannot steal short/point-blank drags for movement'); core/gesture.ts classifyGesture already never returns a move verb, so the fix is scene-side only.
items.implementation_note: Add one INFERRED constant to src/config/gesture.ts (e.g. STROKE_SLOP_WORLD_PX ≈ 4–8 world px, seeded from the OS 4-px convention scaled to world space) and key `mouseMoving` on cumulative displacement from the pointerdown point instead of dragPoints.length; once exceeded, latch 'this gesture is a stroke' until pointerup. finishStroke stays as-is (2-point gate + classifyGesture's degenerate→slash default already satisfy ANY-stroke=slash).
items.stage: now (it fixes an owner-reported misclassification class)

items.title: Capture coalesced pointer samples via Phaser's exposed native event — getCoalescedEvents through Pointer.event
items.claim: Browsers coalesce device input (mice/pens sample 120–1000 Hz) into rAF-aligned pointermove (~60 Hz); fast flicks therefore reach the app as sparse polylines unless getCoalescedEvents() is read on each pointermove — the W3C/MDN-recommended pattern for stroke capture, adopted by shipped ink SDKs (Nutrient). Phaser 3 does not surface coalesced events itself (no mention anywhere in its Pointer API), but `Pointer.event` exposes 'the most recent native DOM Event', so the scene handler can call `p.event.getCoalescedEvents?.()` and push every coalesced position. Support is 'Limited availability' (not Baseline) per MDN, so the optional-chaining fallback to the single point is mandatory. Payoff here: truer red-stroke rendering of fast flicks against the OG trail, and a truer polylineLength for the flick proxy; blade-path HIT detection is less affected because polyline segments already span the gaps.

sources.title: Smoother Interactions on the Web: getCoalescedEvents() — Nutrient (ink SDK vendor)
Phaser Pointer API (event property; 'DOM pointer events can fire faster than the main browser loop')

items.adjudication_reason: DuelScene's pointermove handler currently pushes one world point per Phaser event into dragPoints (cap 2048) — coalesced points slot into the same array with no core/ change; core/gesture.ts and DrawnStroke are point-count agnostic.
items.implementation_note: In the pointermove handler: `for (const ce of (p.event as PointerEvent).getCoalescedEvents?.() ?? [p.event]) push(stageToWorld(...))` — note coalesced clientX/Y need the same stage-px conversion Phaser applies, so scale via the canvas bounds or reuse Phaser's transform helper; keep the 2048 cap. Apply identically in EncounterScene.

items.title: pointerrawupdate — skip it
items.claim: pointerrawupdate dispatches un-coalesced events as fast as JS can handle them, trading main-thread cost for sub-frame latency; MDN and the spec editor's own comparison say to use it only when coalesced pointermove is insufficient, and warn listeners 'can affect performance'. This repo consumes strokes only at pointerup into a fixed-60 Hz Sim, and the OG being recreated is itself a pure 15 fps stepper with zero interpolation (§S24-E 60 fps burst proof) — sub-frame input latency buys nothing measurable toward 1:1 feel, and Phaser's InputManager doesn't listen to the event anyway.

sources.title: pointermove vs pointerrawupdate — Navid Zolghadr (Pointer Events spec editor) demo/explainer

items.adjudication_reason: Ledger §S24-E ('pure 15fps stepper, zero interpolation') plus Sim's fixed-Hz accumulator (src/core/Sim.ts, Spec-fixed FIXED_HZ) mean sub-rAF input latency is below the game's own perceptual floor; coalesced pointermove (item above) already recovers full path completeness.

items.title: $1/$P gesture recognizers do not apply — the net-displacement sector classifier is the correct shape
items.claim: The $-family are instance-based template matchers for symbol vocabularies: $1 resamples a stroke to N points and nearest-neighbor-matches against stored templates; $P treats gestures as unordered point clouds and is explicitly DIRECTION-INVARIANT (its own authors note clockwise vs counterclockwise circles can't be discriminated). The OG's gesture map is four direction sectors where direction IS the meaning (horizontal=slash, up=jump/launch, down=stab — video-confirmed SYNTHESIS §5), so $P is disqualified outright and $1 would add template storage, resampling, and rotation-invariance machinery to answer a question `atan2` already answers. Practitioner consensus matches: $-recognizers are for letter/shape vocabularies, simple angle thresholds for directional swipes.

sources.title: $1 Unistroke Recognizer — Wobbrock et al., UW ACE Lab (primary)

items.adjudication_reason: src/core/gesture.ts classifyGesture (net-displacement angle vs GESTURE_DIAG_DEG sector) already implements the video-confirmed 4-sector map; a template matcher would be churn violating 'simplest change wins' and would import no OG-measured behavior.

items.title: LAUNCH_FLICK length-as-speed proxy: real per-point timestamps are now cheap, but measure the OG's launch discrimination first
items.claim: The config comment's premise ('raw pointer points carry no per-point timestamps in our pipeline') is a pipeline choice, not a platform limit: every PointerEvent — including each coalesced event — carries its own timeStamp, so carrying {x,y,t} instead of {x,y} enables true velocity-based flick detection, the standard in ink/gesture systems. However the OG's actual launch-vs-jump rule (speed? length? both?) has never been measured from the videos, and RESUME_HERE decision #9's own default is 'keep, revisit at Stage 2 feel pass'. Also flag: decision #9's text still says LAUNCH_FLICK_MAX_LEN=90 but src/config/gesture.ts is 75 (world-space conversion, SESSION13 A0) — the RESUME_HERE row is stale.

items.title: Touch-vs-mouse unification: Phaser's pointer abstraction already covers it; only the slop constant would branch if touch becomes a target
items.claim: Phaser 3 unifies mouse and touch into one Pointer API ('you don't have to worry about whether the user is on a desktop with a mouse, or a mobile device with touch'), dispatching the same pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup stream the scenes already consume, and the repo already handles the classic unification trap of off-target releases via pointerupoutside. The one practice delta that would matter later: touch drag thresholds in shipped systems are substantially larger than mouse ones (Windows mouse 4 px vs Android's touch slop of 8dp ≈ 24–32 physical px) because fingers wobble — so IF a touch build ever becomes a goal, the hold slop from the first item should branch on pointerType (available on the native event). For the current desktop Flash-recreation target, one mouse-scale constant is correct.

items.adjudication_reason: DuelScene.create and EncounterScene both listen on Phaser's unified pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup AND pointerupoutside (the Stage-1 audit's swallowed-stroke fix) — no touch-specific code is missing for the current desktop target; the pointerType slop branch is a noted future adaptation, not present work.

dead_ends: No Phaser GitHub issue or PR adding native getCoalescedEvents support was found (searches surfaced only W3C spec-repo issues and the unrelated phaserjs/phaser#6697 about overlapping HTML elements) — hence the Pointer.event escape-hatch route. No research grounding exists for an 'optimal' diagonal sector half-angle (45° is convention, nobody has published a better number), so GESTURE_DIAG_DEG=45 stays INFERRED on feel alone. The MDN fetch returned 'Limited availability / not Baseline' for getCoalescedEvents but not exact current Safari version numbers, so no per-version support claim is made beyond the Nutrient article's older Chrome 74+/Firefox 67+ figures. The ledger's §S24-H adversarial verify row for §S24-C is still [VERDICT PENDING] — the ANY-stroke=slash rule adjudicated against here is the ledger's current leading reading, not yet skeptic-confirmed.
